channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Indonesia’s Rupiah Defense Seen Needing a Rate-Hike Turbocharge
item.description: Bank Indonesia may need to deploy more aggressive measures, including further rate hikes, to sustainably lift the rupiah from near-record lows, according to analysts.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing

item.title: Gold Steadies Near $4,000 as Traders Prepare for Fed Rate Call
item.description: Gold held near $4,000 an ounce as traders prepared for a Federal Reserve decision this week that’s expected to keep interest rates steady.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Dave Lee: Anthropic Brings ‘Anti-Sell’ Strategy to Its IPO
item.description: Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion US Technology Columnist, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss his piece about Anthropic's IPO announcement. Lee writes about the firm's S-1 containing warnings about the company and prospects for humanity as AI technology continues to advance. Lee adds that the filing is described as “a pitch deliberately designed to be unappealing to those who are a poor fit … while appealing to the type of person we want to hire.” Lee speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asian Stocks to Rise on Tech Rebound, Oil Drops: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to rise, tracking gains on Wall Street after Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering filing revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence ahead of big tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s rate decision.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 27
item.description: Oil fell for a second day as stepped-up diplomatic efforts bolstered hopes a broader escalation in the US-Iran war may be averted.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Lorelei Smillie

item.title: Duke’s Mayo CEO: Our Room for Growth Is Substantial
item.description: E. Yuri Hermida, CEO of Duke’s Mayo Company, discussed the company’s name change from Sauer Brands as it enters a new growth chapter. After divesting its spice business, the company is centering its identity on Duke’s Mayo, whose heritage and recipe date to 1917, while also owning Mateo’s Gourmet Salsa. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pimco Scoops Up $4 Billion of Massive SpaceX AI Debt Package
item.description: Pacific Investment Management Co. bought a $4 billion slice of a huge SpaceX financing deal that will help expand its artificial intelligence ambitions, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Laura Benitez

item.title: Jennifer Garner on Expanding Reach of Once Upon a Farm
item.description: Actress Jennifer Garner is also the chief brand officer and co-founder of Once Upon a Farm that makes organic food for babies and children. She talks about her involvement in the business, keeping prices affordable and the introduction of food enhanced with electrolytes. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nucor Profit Beats Estimates as Higher Steel Prices Lift Results
item.description: Nucor Corp. reported third-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street expectations as higher steel prices helped boost profits at the largest US steelmaker.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Lorinc

item.title: Blackstone Data-Center Operator QTS Seeks $800 Million in Private Placement Debt
item.description: QTS, a data-center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is looking to raise around $800 million through a private placement of debt, as Wall Street looks to every corner of global credit to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Emily Graffeo and Preeti Singh

item.title: Schwab CEO Says It's Easy to Find Top Talent in Texas
item.description: Schwab Corp. Chief Executive Officer Rick Wurster says Texas' cost of living, strong universities and tax advantages versus other states have helped the Westlake-based company recruit employees since relocating from San Francisco in 2021. Schwab now has almost 11,000 Texas employees, he tells Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Mum on Investment Grade as It Warns of More Debt
item.description: Anthropic PBC warned it may need to seek more financing sooner than the artificial-intelligence company had anticipated while saying little about its potential path to an investment-grade credit rating in its closely watched IPO filing.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia and Paula Seligson

item.title: We Support Zuckerberg's Vision: Cassidy
item.description: Lauren Cassidy, CIO at Founders 100 ETF, joins Scarlet Fu and Athanasios Psarofagis on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discuss the Founders 100 ETF (ticker: FFF), the possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX, and how Meta is seeking to raise as much as $95B from selling common and preferred stock. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Como os mercados reagiram após a vitória do Lula
item.description: Daniela Milanese conta como os mercados reagiram após a vitória do Lula nas eleições. Com produção de Beatriz Amat, Daniel Carvalho e Patricia Xavier e edição de Mariana Lumy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Universal Music Group Discussed Going Private With Buyout Firms
item.description: Universal Music Group, the world’s largest record company, has discussed going private with a few prominent Wall Street firms, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Shaw and Michelle F. Davis

item.title: AI Funding Drives US High-Grade Bond Sales to Annual Record
item.description: US investment-grade bond sales set an annual record on Monday, as a surge in artificial intelligence spending drives companies to borrow hundreds of billions of dollars.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Kingsbury and Zahra Tayeb

item.title: Colombia Sells $5.2 Billion in New Bonds Amid Fiscal Strain
item.description: Colombia sold a record $5.2 billion in dollar-denominated bonds on Monday as a new administration pledges to rein in the widening budget gap and put the nation’s debt back on a sustainable path.
item.dc:creator: Nicolle Yapur and Maria Elena Vizcaino

item.title: Lula Upset Jolts Brazil Markets, Emerging Assets Sink
item.description: Brazil’s surprise election result dominated emerging-market trading Monday as the country’s stocks, currencies and debt plunged following Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva victory.
item.dc:creator: Kelsey Butler, Heng Xie and Bhaskar Dutta

item.title: Wall Street Week | Rerouting Global Trade, Private Equity Tested, Realizing Cuba’s Potential
item.description: This week, inflation may be edging lower, but as markets push rates higher, the Fed’s 2% inflation target might be a long way off. And, Mexico is building a land-based trade corridor that could give shipping companies more options when traditional channels are disrupted. Plus, as exits slow and borrowing costs rise, the ability of private equity investments to generate returns that beat public markets is less certain. Later, Cuba is promising its biggest market reforms in decades, but investors remain skeptical that the state will truly give up control. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Week | High Stakes Summit, New Zealand's Brain Drain, Stablecoin Adoption, Bubbly Water
item.description: This week, China thinks it's cracked the code on Trump heading into a summit in Beijing. And, what happens when a country's best and brightest travel overseas and stop coming back? Plus, the most useful thing about crypto might be the one nobody's talking about: cheap and fast cross-border payments. Later, the smartest bet in the sparkling water boom might not be on any brand, but on the companies behind them. (Source: Bloomberg)
